site.name: cloudflare-radar
site.summary: cloudflare-radar-clone Clone of the Cloudflare Radar global internet insights dashboard (single-page app). Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Single-page dashboard: top Cloudflare nav + global time / region filters; main area is a grid of cards — global traffic trends, top browsers, device types, protocol distribution, attack trends, Outage Center, Top domains, Top ASNs, etc.; each card has a chart + tooltip + "View more" entry | | `styles.css` | Card grid, chart palette, tooltip, filter bar, dark header | | `script.js` | Chart rendering (SVG / canvas), filter coordination, time-range switching, tab switching, tooltips |

run_plan.goal: Critique and validate the end-to-end UX of the Cloudflare Radar dashboard (single-page app) including global filters, chart interactions/tooltips, search/lookup, export/share, and major adjacent sections (Traffic, Security, Connectivity, Routing, DNS, Reports) across desktop and mobile viewports.
run_plan.summary: Start at the main dashboard (index.html) and verify the core global filters (location, date range, lookup search, add filter/reset, comparison) and that the displayed cards and mini-metrics update coherently. Then validate the primary drill-down interactions: section navigation, chart tabs/options (e.g., HTTP requests/Bytes/Latency/Anomalies, hourly/daily/weekly), tooltips, and the ‘Details’ / ‘View more’ / ‘Inspect’ entry points. Finally, exercise the Share/Export/Search Radar/API/Language/Theme controls and repeat the most important interactions on mobile, focusing on small tap-target risks.
assumptions: The app is a single-page dashboard implemented in index.html with in-page anchors (e.g., #overview, #traffic, #security, #connectivity, #routing, #dns, #reports) and dynamic content driven by script.js.
All critical user actions (filters, tooltips, chart time granularity, details/inspect links, and share/export) are available on index.html as visible controls per prescan interactables.
There are no additional HTML pages to visit beyond index.html for this clone; any ‘view more’ or ‘data explorer’ behavior likely occurs via modals/overlays or in-page updates.
risk_hotspots: index.html top navigation tap targets (Cloudflare Radar home, Overview/Traffic/Security/Connectivity/Routing/DNS/Reports) flagged as small_tap_target in prescan (some as low as 38–50px height/width).
index.html Search Radar input/button and API/EN/Theme controls: small tap targets and potential accessibility/affordance issues.
index.html global filter bar: Location dropdown, Date range dropdown, ‘Add filter’, and ‘Reset’—high risk of state inconsistency or non-obvious behavior.

index.html chart controls/tabs and time granularity (e.g., Hourly/Daily/Weekly and metrics tabs like HTTP requests/Bytes/Latency/Anomalies): risk that tooltips/graphs don’t synchronize with current filters.
index.html cards with ‘Details’, ‘Inspect’, and ‘View more’: risk that these CTAs open non-functional placeholders or modals with broken focus/close behavior (prescan indicates 6 dialogs).
index.html ‘Share’ and ‘Export’ actions: risk of incorrect formatting, missing confirmation, or blocked downloads in this clone.

phases.title: Baseline load + global navigation/section anchoring
phases.objective: Confirm the single-page dashboard loads correctly and that primary section navigation and sidebar/top links move the user to the intended card groups without losing filter context unexpectedly.
key_checks: Verify initial scroll/anchor state: Overview section is present and ‘GLOBAL VIEW’ and ‘OVERVIEW’ sidebar sections are visible.

Click each top nav link (Overview, Traffic, Security, Connectivity, Routing, DNS, Reports) and confirm the relevant card set becomes visible (URL hash changes to match: #overview/#traffic/#security/#connectivity/#routing/#dns/#reports).

Use the left sidebar quick links (e.g., Global Internet trends, Latest reports, HTTP requests, Traffic by type, Domain rankings, Internet outages, Bot traffic, AI crawlers, HTTP DDoS attacks, Layer 3/4 attacks, Attack map, Email security, Quality, Outages) and confirm expected in-page scrolling/section changes.
Toggle theme using the theme control (prescan indicates a toggle theme button) and confirm charts/cards remain readable and not clipped.
exit_criteria: All 7 top nav items (Overview through Reports) successfully navigate to their corresponding sections (hash + visible content match).
At least 8 representative sidebar links scroll to their expected card group locations without wiping active filter selections.
Theme toggle updates styling without breaking layout or chart rendering.

phases.title: Global filters: location, lookup, date range, add/reset, comparison
phases.objective: Validate that the global filter bar controls update displayed metrics/cards consistently and that state changes are understandable and reversible.
key_checks: In the filter bar, change Location from ‘Worldwide’ to another option (and back) and confirm key metric cards (HTTP requests/Mitigated attacks/Median latency/IPv6 traffic) update.
Use Date range dropdown (Last 24 hours) to switch ranges (at least two different options) and confirm charts and the ‘Data updated’/metrics reflect changes coherently.

Use ‘Lookup’ input (placeholder: Domain, IP, ASN, or report) to enter a valid example-like value (e.g., google.com, an ASN-like number, or a report keyword). Confirm resulting search behavior (e.g., updates relevant cards/search results area).
Click ‘Add filter’ and validate that a new filter condition appears and affects the dashboard output; then use ‘Reset’ to clear and confirm a return to baseline.
Toggle ‘Comparison Previous period’ and verify deltas (+%/-%) and/or charts/labels update accordingly.
exit_criteria: Each control (Location, Date range, Lookup, Add filter, Reset, Comparison) produces a visible and consistent state change in the metrics/cards or chart data.
Reset returns the dashboard to a baseline state equivalent to the starting configuration (or clearly documented defaults).

phases.title: Chart interactivity: metric tabs, time granularity, tooltips, chart syncing
phases.objective: Exercise the main chart interaction patterns: switching chart metric tabs, time granularity, and validating tooltips/legend behavior with current filters.
key_checks: For the Traffic card/chart, switch between metric tabs (HTTP requests / Bytes / Latency / Anomalies) and confirm chart visualization and any headline values/labels change.
Switch time granularity (Hourly/Daily/Weekly) and confirm the x-axis/aggregation changes.
Hover (desktop) over chart points/segments to trigger tooltips and verify tooltip content is plausible and not stale after filter changes.
Repeat one metric/tab interaction after applying a different Date range to ensure tooltip/chart data remains synchronized.
exit_criteria: All visible chart metric tabs and time granularity options can be selected without rendering glitches.
Tooltips appear and reflect current filter settings (no stale/incorrect tooltip values after at least one filter change).

phases.title: Card CTAs: Details/View more/Inspect + dialogs
phases.objective: Validate that primary drill-down CTAs open the correct overlays or states, and that modal/dialog usability (open/close, focus) is sound.
key_checks: Click ‘Details’ on at least two metric cards (e.g., HTTP requests card and Mitigated attacks card) and confirm a dialog/overlay opens with additional breakdown.
Click ‘Inspect’ on the Traffic by type card and verify it leads to the correct inspection view/state (or modal) and can be exited cleanly.
Click at least one ‘View more’ entry inside a card (if present) and confirm it navigates or expands content appropriately.
In each opened dialog, verify close behavior (X/escape/backdrop), and that returning to dashboard restores the prior scroll position or active section.
exit_criteria: At least 2–3 CTAs open the expected overlays/states and can be closed reliably.
No broken UI states after closing dialogs (charts still render; cards remain visible).

phases.title: Share/Export/Search Radar/API/Language controls + mobile regression
phases.objective: Validate utility controls and repeat critical UX on mobile to catch tap-target and interaction issues.
key_checks: Click ‘Share’ and confirm link creation/copy UI or share dialog appears (and can be dismissed).
Click ‘Export’ and verify that an export action initiates correctly (download or export dialog).
Use ‘Search Radar’ input and attempt to submit; confirm it routes to the correct results/state (or filters) and handles empty/invalid input gracefully.
Click API and EN controls (language), and verify they don’t break layout or get stuck in menus.
On mobile viewport: repeat Phase 1 (top nav + one sidebar link) and Phase 2 (Date range + Add filter + Reset) interactions; specifically verify tap targets are usable and not mis-tapped.
exit_criteria: Share and Export flows each produce an expected outcome (dialog/confirmation/download or clear error handling).
Search Radar handles at least one valid submission and one invalid/empty submission without UI breakage.
Mobile: all repeated critical controls activate successfully (no persistent misnavigation or overlays blocking the page).

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all known HTML pages (index.html only).
coverage_targets.features: Exercise most visible controls per key page: top nav, sidebar links, theme toggle, global filter bar (location/date/lookup/add/reset/comparison), chart metric tabs, chart granularity, tooltips, and at least 2–3 card CTAs (Details/Inspect/View more), plus Share/Export/Search Radar/API/EN.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat critical checks on mobile viewport: top nav + one sidebar link, filter bar interactions (date range, add filter, reset), and at least one chart interaction to confirm tooltips/tabs remain usable.

notes: The prescan shows 6 dialogs; prioritize opening/closing flows in Phase 4 to validate dialog usability and state restoration.
Because only index.html exists in the prescan, treat all ‘adjacent flows’ as in-page states/modals rather than separate pages; rely on hash changes and overlay behavior for validation.

ux_notes: Clicking the Search Radar input (ux-117) did not show a detectable dismissal/URL or visible change in the tool result feedback (changed=false), so the tested close affordance was not verified by this action.

The screenshot shows the Search Radar modal is open (heading “Search Radar” in a centered dialog) with a clear close (X) control at the top-right of the modal header area; however, this specific action did not demonstrate closing and restoring interactivity behind the modal.

step.objective: Learn whether the Search Radar modal has a reliable, reachable close affordance and whether closing restores interactivity behind it.

ux_notes: Clicking the 'Radar' brand link to dismiss/escape the Search Radar overlay did not work: locator.click timed out because the Search modal remains open and intercepts pointer events (error explicitly states <div id="searchModal" aria-hidden="false" class="search-modal open"> intercepts pointer events).

The page is still usable behind the overlay in terms of visual context, but the overlay is blocking navigation/clicks—so the primary UX issue is modal dismissal/escape affordance not being reachable via the chosen control.
Small-tap-target warnings were observed for multiple top-nav links and the Search Radar trigger, indicating mobile usability risk (e.g., 'Radar' is 107x28px; below mobile 44px guidance).

step.objective: Verify whether the Search Radar modal has a reliable, reachable close control that restores underlying page interactivity (focus/pointer events).

ux_notes: Attempted to click into the modal close-related control (target ux-35), but the click failed due to the Search Radar overlay intercepting pointer events: console/tool log shows the element <div id="searchModal" aria-hidden="false" class="search-modal open"> subtree intercepts pointer events, and the click timed out after 4000ms.

The mobile screenshot shows the Search Radar modal is still open with a visible “X” icon in the search input area; because the click did not succeed, we have not confirmed whether the “X” dismisses the overlay or restores background interactivity.

step.objective: Test whether the Search Radar overlay can be closed via its explicit X control (not the input focus) on mobile, and whether recovery restores dashboard interactivity.

step.success_criteria: After the click, the Search Radar modal overlay should no longer be visible (close icon disappears / #searchModal is removed or aria-hidden becomes true) and the dimming/pointer-blocking behind the modal should be gone.
